name: TX-12
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+11 PVI) with an incumbent running
Goldman's large financial advantage ($1.5M cash, outside support, no opposition spending)
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
No polling or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The baseline of R+15.1 is well supported by the district's R+11 lean, Goldman's incumbency and fundraising dominance, and a prediction market at 94% Republican. With no contrary evidence, I stay essentially at the baseline and call it Safe R.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major scandal or outside spending surge against Goldman, would move this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 12th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+11. Republican incumbent Craig Goldman, first elected in 2024, is running for reelection and holds a clear financial edge, with roughly $1.5 million on hand and modest outside support and no recorded opposition spending. Democrat Angela Rodriguez Prilliman has no reported fundraising figures.

There is no public polling of the race and no expert ratings, so the forecast relies on fundamentals and prediction markets, which give the Republican about a 94 percent chance. The expected margin is roughly fifteen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
